items.title: Manuel Joseph "Moose" Zanco Interview, 1959-11-25
items.q: I guess his, his personality is like Jeff Salsa told me one time.

ctx.x: I tell you, anybody, anybody that did see Joe in action, to me, Joe was the typical old, old, old time jazz musician. He just didn't care. He just wanted to play music. And, uh, I don't know, I've always admired Joe. I like Joe. I like his style. I like the way, maybe I, I would never think of action. I would never think of acting the way Joe acted on a bandstand, you understand? But, I mean, you had to appreciate what he was doing. Everything he did was just part of the show, you know?

I guess his, his personality is like Jeff Salsa told me one time. Jeff is a guy who goes to school, what's he studying? Philosophy? Psychology. Psychology. And, uh, he figured out one time, from talking to, talking and listening to George Gaynor and Jim Robinson, or maybe George talk about Jim, or something about those guys, that, that the old New Orleans style musician wasn't just a style of playing.
It was the character too, I believe. It was an absolute personality. Yeah.
